instructionalProposals.contentQualification: HOLD source-tag union as precise 2.1 actor teaching or complete protocol skill. ARP resolves local/next-hop IPv4 link-layer addresses, not DNS names, end-to-end routes or IPv6 neighbor discovery. Spoofing may enable interception; it does not prove interception of every host, plaintext visibility, attacker identity or universally effective inspection controls. Exact numbered definition scope stays withheld; existing support link is context only.

instructionalProposals.teachingUnderstanding: Recognize ATT&CK as an adversary-behavior reference framework; precise linkage remains withheld until matrix/steps shorthand is qualified.
instructionalProposals.contentQualification: HOLD matrix and attack steps as an exhaustive checklist, fixed chronology, necessary occurrence of every tactic, unique actor identity, confirmed IOC or vulnerability prioritization. Current wording does not explicitly mandate order; this hold prevents that misreading. ATT&CK is a knowledge base/taxonomy: tactics describe goals and techniques methods; its matrix is a representation. Framework naming/source labels/distractor options do not teach all behaviors or objective2.1 attribution.

instructionalProposals.teachingUnderstanding: Recognize distributed availability disruption as narrow 2.4 attack vocabulary; no actor attribution or executed mitigation skill.
instructionalProposals.contentQualification: HOLD many systems as a verified host count inferred from source IPs, mandatory malware botnet, one motive/sponsor or actor class. Distributed direct/reflected traffic and amplification require separate mechanisms; application/service state exhaustion and control selection are not taught by this one sentence. Availability impact does not establish attribution, mitigation effectiveness or recovery mastery. Preserve prior APT distractor/family holds.
